work_item.role: W1 public-evidence discovery and neutral admission

collection_state.note: No equivalent active pass-38 branch or PR was present when this batch was started.

discovery_pass.method: Direction-blind admission of four same-model harness observations from the pinned Mercury Harness Benchmark V1 40-trial matrix. W1 preserves concrete CLI/package versions, fresh-sandbox execution, one-rollout design, task-specific CPU declarations, the CritiqueCode benchmark helper fix, and provider-ledger limitations without ranking or causal interpretation.
discovery_pass.environment: Harbor 0.22.0 + E2B Python SDK 2.46.4; fresh single-container sandbox per trial

source_known_dimensions: same source-reported inception/mercury-2.5-preview model ID through OpenRouter
fresh E2B single-container sandbox per trial
concurrency two with harness order rotated by task
same task-specific CPU declarations across harnesses
concrete source-reported harness versions: CritiqueCode 0.1.13+bench, Claude Code 2.1.259, Oh My Pi 18.1.5 with Bun 1.3.14, OpenCode 1.18.27
explicit_unknown_or_nonidentical_dimensi: exact service-side Mercury 2.5 Preview checkpoint behind OpenRouter
harness-native prompting, context handling, tool strategy and termination behavior intentionally differ
CritiqueCode uses a source-documented benchmark helper fix and local adapter whereas Claude Code and OpenCode use Harbor integrations and Oh My Pi uses a local adapter

provenance_strength.w1_treatment: admit factual externally verified resolution counts while preserving source-class differences, concrete versions, benchmark-specific adapter changes, and provider-accounting limitations

protocol_deviations_and_failures.detail: Each task-harness pair has one canonical rollout. W1 does not infer uncertainty or replicate results.
Eight selected tasks declared 2 CPUs / 4 GB RAM and the two SmolAgents tasks declared 8 CPUs / 8 GB RAM. The experiment is CPU-only but not a fixed-vCPU comparison.

Adapter smoke validation required a five-line positive-budget helper fix in the CritiqueCode E2B extension. The source preserves this tracked change; W1 records it rather than treating it as hidden equivalence.

Only 19 trials have a complete OpenRouter generation ledger; 21 use catalog estimates from recorded tokens, and the provider credential was shared across harnesses. W1 therefore admits resolution only rather than promoting cost comparisons.

non_admission_dispositions.surface: Mercury V1 cost and cost-per-resolved comparisons
non_admission_dispositions.reason: Only 19 of 40 trials have a complete provider generation ledger; the remaining 21 use catalog estimates and the credential was shared across harnesses.
The source explicitly states these are study-defined static selection labels rather than official FeatBench difficulty labels.
V2 uses a different model and a disjoint 20-task block. W1 does not combine or interpret the two studies.
